tweets.text:
Eric on why the best leaders from the last generation keep struggling at scaling AI companies:

"There's just some impedance mismatch between AI founders, the needs of the business, and what these people are bringing.  

I saw it really abruptly with a particular sales leader who we hired who's said, "Hey, we can't hit any of these things."

Because the way that software sales has been taught forever is a quota capacity model. 

In the early days of a company, the quotas are $1.2, $1.5 million. 

Fundamentally, without realizing it, everybody was implementing something that was based on pushing demand, not pulling demand.

And for so many of these companies, there's a new AI-enabled product that comes along and they are selling magic. 

It turns out if you're selling magic and you're the first one there, you're gonna sell a lot more than $2 million.

It turns out that in a lot of these companies, you have reps doing $10, $20, $30 million.

So one of my big things that I started to realize is as I'm interviewing these folks, I say "you need to check everything at the door."

Check all the baggage, check everything that you learned and learn this from first principles."

Dear Readers,

Thank you sincerely for subscribing, commenting, and engaging with my work.

I started Beyond the Ideological because I enjoy developing and reworking concepts (most recently Third Worldism), connecting dots, and sharing things I find intriguing.

Unfortunately, my Substack has grown less organized and less fun than I would like, and I want a structure that is easier for me to sustain and, more importantly, easier for you to follow.

Starting August 15th, you can expect five formats:

1- The Meridian — A weekly column or essay on geopolitics, a crisis, a war, a controversy, or idea consuming the political and intellectual debate of the moment.

2- From Elsewhere — Every Friday, a short note on some developments worth watching across different sectors paired with selected links, books, and excerpts from sources that rarely enter the usual conversation, including Arab and Israeli media and publications from Latin America, Europe, Africa, and beyond.

3- Long Cycles — On the 15th of every month, a closer look at some of the long-term forces reshaping societies beyond the Western world, from political causes, demographics, and migration to technology/A.I. adoption, urbanization, and generational shifts.

4- The Palimpsest — On the 30th of every month, a translated short text from literature, history, or political thought that I believe deserves a wider audience.

5- Beyond the Ideological Podcast — Periodically.

The purpose is to bring together developments too often examined separately and to share more of the background that informs my analysis and conclusions. Geopolitics cannot be separated from markets, energy from industrial capacity, or political movements from the intellectual traditions that animate them. Third Worldism, liberalism, Islamism, technological utopianism, and other ideological doctrines also shape how events are interpreted and which solutions appear desirable. In this sense, I consider Beyond the Ideological a very humble effort to look at both the forces moving the world and the battles over how to understand them.

I hope you will enjoy the next chapter of this project!

https://t.co/s0eCT5psmz

but yeah all that aside, agree you've got to align around holders and that's been a major focus for yuga

GDP as we know it will be obsolete by 2030.

I don't make calls like this lightly, but the way we've measured economies is about to stop working because the equation itself is changing.

You've heard me talk about the magic formula. It comes down to how many people are working, what they're producing, and what they can borrow on top of that. That's the whole story of the economy right there.

But look at what's coming into the equation. Humans are still a big chunk of it but now you've got robots, AI, energy density, and compute efficiency all piled on top. Each one is heading straight up the exponential curve and none of them fit inside the old measure.

By the time you're reading GDP numbers in 2030, they'll be measuring the wrong economy.

This is the Economic Singularity, and it’s coming sooner than most people are ready for. It isn't some far off sci-fi moment… It's something we'll live through inside the next five years.

tweets.text:
Ok friends, sharing the recipe to build basically any agent product:

• Memory: learn everything useful about the user, their work, people, preferences, projects, decisions, etc. from their emails, drive, computer files etc

• Context engineering: figure out which tiny subset of all that memory + current state actually belongs in the context window for the task.

• Skills: teach the agent how to do the work. Build a complex DCF. Prepare a board meeting. Triage an inbox. Run customer research. Write an investment memo.

• Tools / MCPs: give it access to the world. Email, calendar, Slack, GitHub, CRM, browser, databases, internal APIs, computer use, etc.

• Agent runtime: the loop that plans, acts, observes, retries, delegates, checkpoints state and can keep working for hours or days.

• Triggers: cron jobs + events. New email arrives. Meeting ends. Customer churns. Metric changes. Deadline approaches. The agent wakes up without being prompted.
